0.name: LLM Providers & Model APIs
0.description: Configuring and calling large language model providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, xAI, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and others): API keys, model selection, chat and embedding models.

1.name: Agent Frameworks & Runtimes
1.description: Building and running AI agents with a framework or SDK: agent concepts, agent loops, flows, custom and multi-agent setups, and framework integrations. Largest topic; about 43% of files are crewAI docs.

2.name: Agent Memory
2.description: Giving agents memory: storing, searching and recalling memories across sessions, conversation context and compaction, and memory services such as mem0.

3.name: Code Review
3.description: Reviewing code with or for agents: pull request review commands, reviewer agents, review checklists, verification steps and code-quality analysis.

4.name: Authentication & Credentials
4.description: Authentication and authorization: OAuth and SSO setup, access tokens, API keys and cloud secrets for connectors and services, plus identity-security skill templates.

5.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
5.description: Model Context Protocol: building MCP servers and clients, connecting agents to MCP tools, MCP configuration, remote servers and MCP registries.

6.name: Design Systems & Typography
6.description: Visual design guidance: design systems, colors, fonts and typography rules, layout principles and HTML/CSS styling; mostly design-system skills and templates (over half from open-design).

7.name: Observability, Tracing & Telemetry
7.description: Monitoring agent and LLM applications: tracing, telemetry, logging, token and usage tracking, integrations with observability tools, and related privacy notes.

8.name: Market & Geopolitical Data
8.description: Financial and world data for agents: market data, trading and investment analysis skills, economic indicators, and geopolitical monitoring and reports.

9.name: Voice Agents & Speech
9.description: Voice and audio: real-time voice agents, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, telephony (e.g. Twilio) and real-time audio frameworks.

10.name: JavaScript/TypeScript Build Configuration
10.description: JavaScript/TypeScript tooling: bundler and build configuration (Vite, webpack), TypeScript and ESLint settings, package scripts and monorepo migrations (many from nx).

11.name: Browser Automation
11.description: Agents that control a web browser: browser sessions, cloud browsers, browser automation tools and their request options (e.g. Skyvern, agent-browser, crewAI automation tools).

12.name: Messaging Channels & Chat Bots
12.description: Connecting agents to chat platforms: Slack, Telegram, Discord, Microsoft Teams, WeChat, IRC and other channels, including bots, webhooks and conversation sessions.

13.name: Cybersecurity
13.description: Security operations and testing: threat detection, SIEM queries (e.g. Splunk), vulnerability and malware analysis, penetration testing and security standards. About 75% of files are from Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills.

14.name: React & Frontend Components
14.description: Frontend UI development: React components and hooks, state management, component libraries, design tokens and React best-practice rules.

15.name: Docker & Kubernetes Deployment
15.description: Installing and deploying applications: Docker and Docker Compose, Kubernetes and Helm, Terraform and cloud self-hosting guides.

16.name: Video Production & Animation
16.description: Creating videos and animations with agents: video composition, scenes, transitions, subtitles, rendering pipelines and animation techniques (mostly OpenMontage and HyperFrames).

17.name: Testing
17.description: Software testing: test setup and infrastructure, unit, integration and end-to-end tests, test-driven development and verification strategies.

18.name: Agent Skills
18.description: Agent skills as a format: writing, structuring, installing and publishing SKILL.md skill packages, skill metadata and skill catalogs.

19.name: Scheduling & Task Queues
19.description: Running agent work over time: scheduled and cron tasks, reminders, background and asynchronous execution, checkpointing, and pausing for human feedback.

20.name: Mixed: Runtime Internals
20.description: Mixed topic without one clear theme: internal engineering notes on sync, queues, retries, worker services and crashes, plus triage reports and release notes. Interpret with caution.

21.name: Vector Stores & Embeddings
21.description: Retrieval infrastructure: vector databases and stores, embeddings, vector search and knowledge bases used for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

22.name: Agent Personas & Roles
22.description: Role definitions for specialist agents: persona, identity, expertise, mission and success metrics (e.g. marketing strategist, engineer, analyst); mostly from agency-agents.

23.name: Plugins & Extensions
23.description: Extending agent platforms with plugins: plugin structure, creation, SDKs, capabilities and distribution, including plugin-level AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md guidance.

24.name: Sandboxes & Isolated Execution
24.description: Running agent code safely: sandboxes and isolated execution environments, sandbox policies and permissions, containers and code-interpreter tools (e.g. Daytona, E2B).

25.name: Release & Version Management
25.description: Shipping releases: release workflows and branches, version tags, publishing and update processes, and provider release changelogs (notably Apache Airflow).

26.name: Agent Chat UI & Agent-User Interaction
26.description: Chat interfaces between users and agents: chat components, shared agent state, generative UI and the AG-UI protocol. About 72% of files are CopilotKit docs and demos.

27.name: Model Training & Distributed Inference
27.description: Training and serving models: fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, distributed training and parallelism, inference engines and model benchmark reports.

28.name: Email & Workspace Agents
28.description: Agents that work with email and office workspaces: reading, sending and organizing email (Gmail, Outlook, IMAP) and Google Workspace skills.

29.name: Web Search & Scraping Tools
29.description: Web search, research and scraping tools for agents (e.g. Tavily, SerpApi, Firecrawl). About 87% of files are crewAI tool docs repeated across documentation versions.

30.name: Repo-specific: agno Cookbook Test Logs
30.description: Repository-specific: test logs and READMEs for agno's cookbook examples. Not a general theme.

31.name: Deep Research Agents
31.description: Agents that research topics autonomously: deep research workflows, researcher agents, web and paper research, and generating research reports.

32.name: Microservices (go-micro)
32.description: Microservice architecture and service agents: services, service discovery, gRPC and gateways; mostly from go-micro.

33.name: Building from Source & Native Builds
33.description: Building projects from source: language toolchains (e.g. Rust), native binaries, platform-specific setup for macOS and Linux, and packaging.

34.name: Evaluation, Benchmarks & Performance
34.description: Measuring agents and systems: evaluation frameworks, scorers and LLM judges, benchmark suites, and performance testing and optimization.

37.name: Documentation Writing
37.description: Documentation about documentation: skills and agents that write or maintain docs, documentation-site setup, docs contribution rules and doc templates.

38.name: Implementation Plans & Specs
38.description: Planning work before or during execution: implementation plans, specifications, task breakdowns, codebase exploration, and agent planning and reasoning features.

39.name: Translation & i18n
39.description: Internationalization: translation guidelines and glossaries, locale files, i18n libraries and translator agents.

40.name: Repo-specific: agent-zero Module Docs
40.description: Repository-specific: agent-zero's per-module documentation (.dox.md and AGENTS.md files describing each module's purpose and ownership). Not a general theme.

42.name: REST & OpenAPI APIs
42.description: HTTP APIs: API references, OpenAPI specifications, REST endpoints, server adapters and API inventories.
